content_voiceover: This is the Taiwan MPN Working Group algorithm for essential thrombocythemia, which uses a four tier risk system rather than the simpler two tier system used in PV. Very low risk means no thrombosis history, age sixty or under, and JAK2 V617F un-mutated, these patients need no cardiovascular risk factors to simply be observed, or get aspirin if cardiovascular risk factors are present. Low risk is the same age and thrombosis criteria but with JAK2 mutation present, these patients generally receive aspirin. Intermediate risk means age over sixty without JAK2 mutation, managed with aspirin if symptomatic with cardiovascular risk factors, or observation if asymptomatic without those risk factors, since hydroxyurea is not generally recommended in this asymptomatic subgroup. High risk is defined by a history of arterial or venous thrombosis at any age, or age over sixty combined with JAK2 mutation, these patients need hydroxyurea plus aspirin as the backbone regimen. For high risk patients with arterial thrombosis history, consider twice daily aspirin or another antiplatelet; for venous thrombosis history, add systemic anticoagulation. If hydroxyurea fails due to intolerance or resistance, anagrelide is the next option. Peginterferon alfa two a or two b is noted as another option, though not yet TFDA approved in Taiwan. Note the two footnoted cautions, avoid aspirin in acquired von Willebrand disease or platelet counts at or above fifteen hundred times ten to the ninth per liter.
keypoints: Four risk tiers in ET, very low, low, intermediate, and high, based on age, thrombosis history, and JAK2 status
Very low risk without cardiovascular risk factors can simply be observed without aspirin
High risk, defined by prior thrombosis or age over sixty plus JAK2 mutation, gets hydroxyurea plus aspirin
Anagrelide is the second line option for hydroxyurea intolerance or resistance
Avoid aspirin in acquired von Willebrand disease or platelet count fifteen hundred times ten to the ninth or higher
keypoint_voiceover: ET risk stratification is more granular than PV, splitting into four tiers using age, thrombosis history, and JAK2 mutation status. The practical takeaway is that JAK2 mutation status shifts management even within the same age and thrombosis category, and very high platelet counts should prompt caution before starting aspirin due to acquired von Willebrand risk.
